group.title: Jobs
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A person who grows food or keeps animals on a farm.
wrong: The farmer flies planes all day.

words.meaning: A person who makes food, often as a job.
wrong: The cook drives the school bus.

words.meaning: A person who sings, often as a job.
wrong: The singer never makes a sound.

words.meaning: A person who plays a part in a film or a play.
examples: The {actor} is in a new film.
wrong: The actor builds houses for a living.

words.meaning: A woman who plays a part in a film or a play.
examples: The {actress} won a prize for her film.
wrong: The actress fixes cars at the garage.

words.meaning: A person who paints or draws pictures.
wrong: The artist never draws or paints.

words.meaning: A person who writes books or stories.
wrong: The writer can’t read or write.

words.meaning: A person who makes bread and cakes to sell.
examples: The {baker} gets up at four to make bread.
wrong: The baker sells shoes and coats.

words.meaning: A person who dances, often as a job.
wrong: The dancer sits still all day.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to clean houses or offices.
wrong: The cleaner makes the rooms dirty.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to build houses.
examples: The {builder} is making a new wall.
wrong: The builder teaches music at school.

words.meaning: A person who plans and makes machines, roads or bridges.
examples: The {engineer} is planning a new bridge.
wrong: The engineer looks after babies at home.

words.meaning: A person who studies how the world works.
wrong: The scientist sells fruit at the market.

words.meaning: A doctor for animals.
examples: We took our sick cat to the {vet}.
wrong: The vet is a doctor for cars.

words.meaning: A person in an office who answers calls and writes letters.
wrong: The secretary drives a fire truck.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to cut and wash hair.
wrong: The hairdresser fixes my teeth.

words.meaning: A person who paints walls or pictures.
wrong: The painter never uses paint.

words.meaning: A person who takes photos, often as a job.
wrong: The photographer has no camera.

words.meaning: A person who plays music.
wrong: The musician can’t play any music.

words.meaning: A person who works in an army.
wrong: The soldier sells cakes in a bakery.

words.meaning: A person who does a job.
wrong: The workers never do any work.

words.meaning: A person who works at a desk in an office.
examples: The {office worker} uses a computer all day.
wrong: The office worker works on a boat at sea.

words.meaning: A person who meets visitors at the front desk.
examples: The {receptionist} gave me my room key.
wrong: The receptionist works in a field with cows.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to drive a bus.
examples: The {bus driver} stopped at our street.
wrong: The bus driver flies a plane.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to drive people in a taxi.
examples: The {taxi driver} took us to the airport.
wrong: The taxi driver rides a horse to work.

words.meaning: A person who brings letters to your home.
examples: The {mail carrier} brought me a letter.
wrong: The mail carrier cooks food in a restaurant.

words.meaning: A person who catches fish as a job.
examples: The {fisherman} goes to sea in a small boat.
wrong: The fisherman catches birds in the sky.

words.meaning: A person who looks after a garden.
wrong: The gardener works only under the sea.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to watch and keep a place safe.
examples: A {guard} stands at the bank door.
wrong: The guard helps robbers take the money.

words.meaning: A person who works in a library.
examples: The {librarian} helped me find a book.
wrong: The librarian works in a car shop.

words.meaning: A person who travels into space.
wrong: The astronaut never leaves the ground.

words.meaning: A person who writes code for computers.
wrong: The programmer never uses a computer.

words.meaning: A person who has a small shop.
wrong: The shopkeeper teaches in a school.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to sell things.
examples: The {salesperson} showed me a new phone.
wrong: The salesperson never sells anything.

words.meaning: A person who works on a ship.
examples: The {sailor} is on a ship at sea.
wrong: The sailor works deep under the ground.

words.meaning: A person who finds news for TV or newspapers.
examples: The {reporter} talked to people in the street.
wrong: The reporter never tells anyone the news.

words.meaning: A person who looks after animals in a zoo.
wrong: The zookeeper works in a bank.

words.meaning: A person who keeps swimmers safe at a pool or beach.
wrong: The lifeguard sleeps while the children swim.

words.meaning: A person with a funny face and clothes who makes people laugh.
wrong: The sad clown makes everyone cry.

words.meaning: A person whose job is to look after children in their home.
examples: The {nanny} takes the kids to the park.
wrong: The nanny looks after cars.
